findings.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:460 — The async forEach callback adds deletion promises only after awaiting getCalendar, allowing Promise.all(apiDeletes) to run too early and leave recurring calendar updates or deletions unfinished or lost.

packages/app-store/index.ts:3 — Calling every import() while constructing appStore eagerly loads all app packages, preserving startup overhead instead of loading only the selected app through deferred loader functions.

goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/index.ts:3 — Calling every import() while constructing appStore eagerly loads all app packages, preserving startup overhead instead of loading only the selected app through deferred loader functions.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the refactored code in packages/app-store/index.ts creates an object where each property is an import() call that executes immediately when the module is loaded. While import() returns a Promise (enabling async loading), all the import() calls are invoked at module initialization time, not when the specific app is accessed. This means all app modules start loading in parallel at startup rather than being truly lazy-loaded on demand. A more effective lazy-loading pattern would use getter functions or a factory pattern. This is a valid architectural concern about the implementation not achieving its apparent goal of reducing startup overhead.
